name: Minnesota veterans: accredited claims help
organization: Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs and County Veterans Service Offices
description: Free help from your County Veterans Service Officer and the Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits, plus state benefits. Every Minnesota county has a veterans service office.
next_step: Choose your county for its Veterans Service Office, or call MDVA’s one-stop line, 1-888-LinkVet (888-546-5838), seven days a week. For a state claims officer, the St. Paul Claims Office is 612-970-5662 and the Fargo Claims Office, which assists northwest Minnesota, is 701-451-4640.
constraints: Hours differ by office; some counties are open only part of the week, so call first.
Minnesota has Tribal Veterans Service Officers, listed by the state department; they are not shown on county cards.

name: Minnesota Aging Pathways (formerly the Senior LinkAge Line)
description: Minnesota’s free statewide aging line, run by the Board on Aging with the area agencies on aging. It is the state’s long-term care options counseling service and its Aging and Disability Resource Center for older adults, and it helps with housing, transportation, meals, in-home help and Medicare. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 800-333-2433, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or choose a county above for its area agency on aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Minnesota
organization: Minnesota Board on Aging, Minnesota Aging Pathways
description: Free, unbiased help with Medicare choices, enrollment and costs. Minnesota Aging Pathways is the state’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP).
next_step: Call 800-333-2433, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: The line is a telephone and chat service; for a plan decision, have your Medicare card and your drug list ready.

source_evidence.title: Minnesota Aging Pathways: Medicare
source_evidence.scope: SHIP status, hours and free counseling; search excerpt.

name: Minnesota Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Minnesota Board on Aging, Office of Ombudsman for Long-Term Care
description: Statewide advocacy for people in nursing homes, boarding care homes, assisted living, customized living, foster care and home care, delivered by regional ombudsmen and, in some places, certified volunteers.
next_step: Call 800-657-3591 (toll-free) or 651-431-2555, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and give the county and facility name. To report suspected abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of a vulnerable adult, call the Minnesota Adult Abuse Reporting Center at 844-880-1574, 24 hours a day. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

name: Free legal help for Minnesota veterans
organization: Minnesota Assistance Council for Veterans (Vetlaw); LawHelpMN
description: The Minnesota Assistance Council for Veterans’ Vetlaw program gives Minnesota veterans free legal information, referrals and advice on most legal topics and holds legal clinics across the state. LawHelpMN.org explains civil legal issues and helps you find your local legal aid program.
next_step: Call Vetlaw at 651-200-4750 or email vetlaw@mac-v.org to schedule time with a staff attorney, or ask about the next clinic near you.
constraints: Vetlaw attorneys advise on Minnesota state law only, not federal law or other states’ law.
Most free veteran legal aid programs screen by income, case type and location; Vetlaw will help you see which you qualify for.

name: VA health care systems serving Minnesota
description: Minnesota veterans are served mainly by the Minneapolis VA Health Care System (medical center at One Veterans Drive, Minneapolis, 612-725-2000, with 15 locations in Minnesota and western Wisconsin) and the St. Cloud VA Health Care System (medical center at 4801 Veterans Drive, 320-252-1670, with clinics in Brainerd, Alexandria and Montevideo). The association’s health care page also names Sioux Falls among the medical centers Minnesota veterans can use.
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves a county depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.

Duluth office: 118 East Superior St., Suite 100, Duluth, MN 55802, 218-625-1400.

name: Minnesota Assistance Council For Veterans: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 19-MN-046): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
